explainability.title: Modern IKEv2 Protocol Engine (RFC 7296)
explainability.plain_english_summary: Manages your VPN connection lifecycle with high speed, instant auto-reconnect, and seamless network mobility across Wi-Fi and 5G.
explainability.detailed_explanation: IKEv2 acts as the intelligent digital negotiator for your VPN. Imagine traveling on a train where your laptop switches between station Wi-Fi and 5G cellular—older VPNs would freeze or crash, forcing you to log in again. IKEv2 natively uses MOBIKE (RFC 4555) technology to instantly shift your encrypted session between network connections without dropping active video calls or web apps. Additionally, it uses a streamlined 4-message exchange (IKE_SA_INIT & IKE_AUTH) with built-in cookie challenges to protect your server against hacker overload (DoS SYN-flood) attacks.

explainability.title: Obsolete 3DES-CBC Cipher (Vulnerable to Sweet32 Collision Attacks)
explainability.plain_english_summary: Obsolete 1990s 64-bit encryption block cipher that modern high-speed computers can break through data collision attacks.
explainability.detailed_explanation: Triple-DES scrambles data by running the 1970s DES algorithm 3 times in sequence. However, because it uses tiny 64-bit blocks of data, modern security research (Sweet32 attack / CVE-2016-2183) proves that an eavesdropper capturing around 32GB of high-speed VPN traffic can mathematically break the encryption and recover secret plaintext data. Formally retired and forbidden by NIST SP 800-131A guidelines.

explainability.title: Cryptographic Key Agreement (DH Group Standard)
explainability.plain_english_summary: Mathematical method allowing VPN endpoints to securely agree on session keys.
explainability.detailed_explanation: Protects key distribution so adversaries watching network traffic cannot deduce session encryption keys for DH Group unknown.

explainability.title: PFS Disabled (Retroactive Decryption Exposure)
explainability.plain_english_summary: CRITICAL RISK: Data session keys depend on the master server key—stealing the server key allows hackers to decrypt all recorded past traffic.
explainability.detailed_explanation: Without PFS, session keys for data traffic depend directly on the main initial master key of the VPN tunnel. If an adversary records encrypted network traffic today and later compromises the VPN gateway's private key, they can retroactively decrypt all historical captured data.

explainability.title: IPsec Tunnel Mode Encapsulation (Complete Outer IP Envelope)
explainability.plain_english_summary: Encloses your entire original IP packet—including private source and destination IP addresses—inside a brand-new encrypted outer IP envelope.
explainability.detailed_explanation: Think of Transport Mode as sending a postcard where the message is written in code, but the sender and recipient home addresses are clearly visible on the outside. Tunnel Mode is like placing that entire postcard inside a thick, opaque courier envelope addressed only between two secure VPN gateways. Eavesdroppers, ISPs, or hackers monitoring public internet routers cannot see your internal company IP addresses, device names, or network architecture—they only see encrypted traffic traveling between the two public gateway endpoints.

explainability.title: AI Behavioral Pattern Recognition (VPN-FT Application)
explainability.plain_english_summary: Machine Learning identified the exact application activity ('VPN-FT') inside the VPN tunnel using behavioral traffic patterns without breaking encryption.
explainability.detailed_explanation: Even though your VPN tunnel scrambles 100% of your data packets into unreadable noise, different applications leave distinct physical signatures in how they communicate. Our trained XGBoost Machine Learning model analyzed 28 non-encrypted flow characteristics—such as packet size variations, transmission timing intervals, and bandwidth burst ratios. Like a detective identifying a person by the cadence of their footsteps without seeing their face, the AI correctly identified your tunnel activity as 'VPN-FT' with 27.3% statistical confidence, zero decryption required.

explainability.title: Observable Network Metadata Analysis (192.168.1.10 -> 10.0.0.1)
explainability.plain_english_summary: Assessed outer IP header visibility, unencrypted IKE identity payloads, SPI correlation risk, and Transport mode exposure (Rating: LOW).
explainability.detailed_explanation: Even when payload content is encrypted, eavesdroppers can perform side-channel traffic analysis using unencrypted metadata. Our metadata analyzer inspected outer endpoint IP pairs (192.168.1.10 -> 10.0.0.1), verified whether identity payloads ($ID_i$/$ID_r$) were transmitted in cleartext, and evaluated cleartext ESP Security Parameter Index (SPI) linkability risks. Current exposure score is 15/100.

known_limitations.reason: IKEv2 SA lifetime is negotiated in IKE_AUTH payloads which are encrypted after the IKE_SA_INIT exchange. It cannot be extracted from a PCAP without the pre-shared key or private key for decryption.

A CREATE_CHILD_SA exchange with a Diffie-Hellman KE payload can be observed in some captures, but its absence does not prove PFS is disabled and its presence does not establish the endpoint's enforcement policy.
The ESP sequence number is visible in the ESP header, but the configured anti-replay window and enforcement behavior are not established by observing sequence numbers alone.
